evidence_title: Quantitative Historical Change in Bumblebee (Bombus spp.) Assemblages of Red Clover Fields

evidence_notes:
Figure 3 (PDF p. 5) provides area-standardized abundance (bees/m²) for early, middle and late clover flowering seasons in the historical and modern surveys. Within each species panel, digitized vertical distances from zero are [3.288000000000011, 0.9390000000000214, 10.334000000000003] for the past and [5.166499999999985, 10.334000000000003, 17.850000000000023] for the present, in PDF points. The same linear y-axis factor applies to both periods and cancels: RR = sum(present distances)/sum(past distances). This gives equal weight to all three seasons and retains zero seasonal observations. d = RR−1 and yi = ln(RR). N = 211 comprises 70 historical and 141 modern field-day records (Table 1); vi = 1/211 is the project working proxy. Vector coordinates are read to approximately 0.01 PDF points.

Data-source reference: Dupont, YL, Damgaard, C, Simonsen, V (2011). Quantitative Historical Change in Bumblebee (Bombus spp.) Assemblages of Red Clover Fields. PLoS ONE 6:e25172. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0025172

evidence_notes:
Figure 7 (PDF p. 7, printed p. 180) reports first-generation male catch in moths per trap-night on the original scale. The first and last black bars, seasons 1992–93 and 2014–15, are digitized as approximately 18.3 and 1.1 moths per trap-night (reading precision approximately ±0.2). RR = 1.1/18.3; d = RR−1; yi = ln(RR). The first generations correspond to spring 1992 and spring 2014, a 22-year interval. N = 248 retains the documented site-season observations for the first-generation series (Table 3, total df 247); vi = 1/248 is the project working proxy. The endpoint ratio is calculated directly from original-scale rates, separately from the log(x+1) regression coefficients.

Data-source reference: Baker, GH, Tann, CR (2017). Long-term changes in the numbers of Helicoverpa punctigera (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae) in a cotton production landscape in northern New South Wales, Australia. Bulletin of Entomological Research 107:174–187. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0007485316000821

evidence_notes:
PDF5/1051 Results, paragraph beginning "The largest number of cavities". Fraction of initially occupied cavities remaining active. Baseline = 79, endpoint = 37; corresponding exposure denominators = 1 and 1. RR = ((37+0)/1)/((79+0)/1); d = RR−1; yi = ln(RR). N = 79 represents 79 initially occupied cavities. vi = 0.014368799178925763, calculated from the binomial retained-active fraction. The authors report that 42 of 79 occupied cavities became inactive between 1995 and 1996; 37/79 remained active. For this single-cohort retained fraction, delta-method var[ln(p)] = (1−p)/(79p) = 1/37−1/79. The cavity cohort, rather than the separately tabulated mitotype sample totals, defines this response.

Data-source reference: Pinto, M. A., Rubink, W. L., Coulson, R. N., Patton, J. C., Johnston, J. S. (2004). Temporal pattern of Africanization in a feral honeybee population from Texas inferred from mitochondrial DNA. Evolution58(5):1047–1055. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.0014-3820.2004.tb00438.x

Danaus plexippus was recorded in association with flowers of Epidendrum paniculatum (as reported; species complex possible) (PDF2–4/193–195， Of all the plants growing there we moved the orchid plant). Reference: Wagner, W.H. Jr. (1973). An orchid attractant for monarch butterflies (Danaidae). Journal of the Lepidopterists’ Society 27(3):192–196.

Janes, Genevieve E. van der Voort, Dezene P. W. Huber (2024). We know very little about pollination in the Platanthera Rich (Orchidaceae: Orchidoideae).
